items.why: AI Voice Agents usage table and a pricing summary were added, but the per-minute rate, bundles and 50 included minutes were already on the page.
A comparison-table row label was renamed from Extra usage to Usage credits with no change in values.
A webinar banner at the top of the page was removed; no pricing changed.
Marketing headline and call-to-action copy were reworded; no prices or allowances changed.
Reference credit consumption for Bits Investigate fell from ~6.5 to ~4 credits, and Kafka Console pricing now explicitly excludes Confluent Cloud.

record.short: Bits Investigate autonomous investigation now averages ~4 credits instead of ~6.5.
record.headline: Datadog lowered the average credit consumption listed for Bits Investigate from ~6.5 to ~4 credits and dropped Confluent Cloud from Kafka Console pricing.
rows: Self-hosted, Confluent Cloud, Amazon MSK provisioned
record.who: Customers using Bits Investigate with AI credits; Confluent Cloud users are no longer billed for Kafka Console.
record.read: A lower credit count per investigation makes the same AI feature cheaper to run, which may signal falling model costs or a push to drive adoption. The Kafka Console wording moves Confluent Cloud outside the billed scope.
record.caveat: The page says credit figures are averages for reference only and actual consumption varies with task complexity and context.

items.why: Startup and migration credit banners moved higher on the page and a number gained a thousands separator (3000 → 3,000); no change in substance.
Pro Team seat prices shown fell from $29 / $23 to $17 / $13 per seat per month, reversing the increase recorded in week 42.

record.short: Pro Team seat prices shown went from $29 / $23 to $17 / $13 per seat per month.
record.headline: Scribe cut the two Pro Team per-seat prices on its pricing page from $29 and $23 to $17 and $13 per month, still starting at 5 seats.
rows: Pro Team, per seat per month (first price)
Pro Team, per seat per month (second price)
record.who: Pro Team customers and prospects; it is unclear whether existing subscribers move to the new price.
record.read: This undoes much of the +77% rise seen two weeks earlier, so the earlier increase may have been tested and rolled back. The 5-seat minimum stays, which keeps small teams on Pro Personal.
record.caveat: The page lists two prices without labelling them; they are most likely monthly and annual billing.

items.why: The Enterprise card was reformatted into an Includes list with a Needs additional subscription note; no price or allowance is stated.
Starter monthly price fell from $29 to $19, yearly Starter from $18 to $14 and yearly Pro from $64 to $59 per month, with new first-month offers.

record.short: Starter monthly price $29 → $19; yearly Starter $18 → $14 and yearly Pro $64 → $59 per month.
record.headline: Synthesia lowered Starter to $19 a month and yearly Starter and Pro to $14 and $59 a month, and added first-month offers of $9 and $49.
record.who: New buyers of Starter and Pro; Pro monthly stays at $89 after the first month.
record.read: Cheaper entry pricing plus a discounted first month points to a push for self-serve conversion against cheaper AI video rivals. The yearly framing also moved from Save up to 3 months to Save up to 4 months.
record.caveat: Pro monthly price is unchanged at $89 after the $49 first month; first-month offers may be time-limited.

items.why: The Professional card lost its description and feature list while price and plan structure stayed the same, which looks like a rendering change.
Only the accurate-as-of date on the Balance earnings footnote differed between the two versions; no pricing changed.
